solution: Normal to \(P_1\): \((2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\times(4\hat{j}-3\hat{k})=-18\hat{i}\); to \(P_2\): \((\hat{j}-\hat{k})\times(3\hat{i}+3\hat{j})=3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\). \(\vec{A}\propto(-18\hat{i})\times(3\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-3\hat{k})=54(-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\), so take \(\vec{A}=-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\). Then \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{(-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})}{\sqrt{2}\cdot3}=\dfrac{-3}{3\sqrt{2}}=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\) (the opposite direction \(-\vec{A}\) would give \(\frac{\pi}{4}\), which is not offered). Matches option D.

solution: \[\begin{matrix} & L = \frac{x + 1}{3} = \frac{y + 3}{5} = \frac{z + 5}{7} \\ & PQ = \frac{x - \frac{15}{7}}{1} = \frac{y - \frac{32}{7}}{4} = \frac{z - 7}{7} = \lambda \end{matrix}\] \[\Rightarrow Q\left( \lambda + \frac{15}{7},4\lambda + \frac{32}{7},7\lambda + 7 \right)\] Since Q lies on line L \[\begin{matrix} & \text{~So,~}\frac{\lambda + \frac{15}{7} + 1}{3} = \frac{7\lambda + 7 + 5}{7} \\ & \ \Rightarrow 7\lambda + 22 = 21\lambda + 36 \\ & \ \Rightarrow \lambda = - 1 \\ & \ \therefore\text{~Point~}Q\left( \frac{8}{7},\frac{4}{7},0 \right) \\ & PQ = \sqrt{\left( \frac{15}{7} - \frac{8}{7} \right)^{2} + \left( \frac{32}{7} - \frac{4}{7} \right)^{2} + (7 - 0)^{2}} = \sqrt{1 + 16 + 49} \\ & PQ = \sqrt{66} \\ & \ \Rightarrow (PQ)^{2} = 66 \end{matrix}\]
note: the z term was written (7 - 0) without the square (as printed that gives 24); it is (7 - 0)^2 = 49, so 1 + 16 + 49 = 66. Key C unchanged.

solution: The line is \(\overline{r} = ( - 3,2,3) + \lambda(3,3, - 1)\), so a point on it is \(M( - 3 + 3\lambda,2 + 3\lambda,3 - \lambda)\) and \(\overline{PM} = (3\lambda - 7,3\lambda - 4,5 - \lambda)\). For the foot, \(\overline{PM} \cdot (3,3, - 1) = 0\): \(3(3\lambda - 7) + 3(3\lambda - 4) - 1(5 - \lambda) = 0\Rightarrow 19\lambda = 38 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2\). So \(M = (3,8,1)\) and \(PM = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{14}\).
